unit.title: Tool calling in code
unit.description: Tool definitions, JSON Schema, tool results, stop reasons, the agent loop, step limits, risky actions

cards.definition: A name, a description and a JSON schema of parameters that you send to the model, so it knows what it may ask your code to do.
cards.example: get_weather(city: string): current weather for a city.

cards.definition: A standard way to describe the shape of JSON data: field names, types and which fields are required. Models use it to produce valid arguments.
The output of the function your code ran, sent back to the model in the next message so it can continue its work.
cards.example: The weather function returns 18 C and cloudy; the model then writes its answer.

cards.definition: A field of the API answer saying why the model stopped: it finished, it hit max_tokens, or it is waiting for a tool to be run.
cards.example: A stop reason of tool use means: run the tool, then call the model again.

cards.definition: The plain-language text telling the model when and how to use a tool; vague descriptions are the first cause of wrong tool calls.
cards.example: Search the internal help center. Use it for product questions, never for orders.

cards.definition: An action that gives the same result if it runs twice, like reading a file. Sending an email is not idempotent, so retries need care.
cards.example: Retrying a failed read is safe; retrying a payment may charge twice.

cards.definition: A loop that calls the model, runs any tool it asks for, appends the result and calls again, until it answers without a tool or a step limit is hit.
cards.example: for step in range(10) stops the loop after 10 steps at most.

exercises.prompt: You declared this tool. A user asks "Is it raining in Lyon?". What does the model produce?
choices: A request to call get_weather with city set to Lyon
It goes online and reads the weather itself
A new JSON schema for another tool
Nothing: tools only work in weather apps
exercises.explain: The model only asks: it outputs the tool name and its arguments. Your code decides whether to run it and sends the result back.

choices: Your code, on your side
The model, on its own servers
The user, by hand
The browser of the provider
exercises.explain: This is the key point of tool calling: the model proposes, your code executes. That is also where you put checks, limits and approvals.

exercises.prompt: Put a tool call round trip in order.
steps: Send the question and the list of tools
The model answers with a tool request
Your code sends the tool result back
The model writes the final answer
exercises.explain: This round trip can repeat several times in one task: that repetition is the agent loop.

exercises.prompt: The model keeps calling search_docs when users ask about their order status. What should you fix first?
choices: The tool descriptions: say clearly when to use each tool
Raise the temperature so it tries other tools
Remove every tool except one
Pay for a larger context window
exercises.explain: Models choose tools from their names and descriptions. A precise description (when to use it, when not to) fixes most wrong choices.

exercises.prompt: This agent loop can run forever and burn the whole budget. Which line should change?
exercises.explain: Replace while True with a bounded loop such as for step in range(10), and stop with a clear message when the limit is hit. Add a cost budget too.

exercises.prompt: Even with a JSON schema, your code should validate the arguments the model sends before running a tool.
exercises.explain: True: the schema guides the model but does not prove the values are sensible or allowed. Check ranges, rights and formats like any user input.

exercises.prompt: Which tool should wait for a human confirmation before it runs?
choices: send_invoice_email
read_calendar
search_docs
get_weather
exercises.explain: Actions that are visible to others, cost money or cannot be undone go through a human checkpoint. Reading data does not need one.

exercises.prompt: A tool fails because the city does not exist. What should your code send back to the model?
choices: A clear error message as the tool result, so it can recover
Nothing: stop the program without a word
Made-up weather, so the answer looks complete
The full Python traceback, shown to the user
exercises.explain: A readable error (city not found, try another spelling) lets the model ask the user or retry correctly. Silent failures and fake data cause wrong answers.

exercises.prompt: MCP lets the same tool server be used by several AI apps, instead of rewriting each tool for each app.
exercises.explain: True: an MCP server exposes tools and data through one standard protocol, and any compatible client (Claude, ChatGPT, IDE agents) can use it.

exercises.prompt: The network failed right after send_email was called. Is it safe to retry automatically?
choices: Not blindly: check first, or use an idempotency key
Yes, retrying a call is always safe
No, no action can ever be retried
Only if the temperature is set to 0
exercises.explain: Sending is not idempotent. Check the sent status, or give each action a unique key so the service ignores duplicates.
